routes.name: Avalanche Gulch
routes.best_season: Climb it from April through June, occasionally into July, while the gulch is still filled with snow. Once the snow melts out the route becomes loose scree and talus and rockfall increases dramatically, so late-season climbs are discouraged.
routes.overview: The standard and most-climbed route on Mount Shasta, a long snow climb gaining about 7,000 vertical feet from Bunny Flat to the 14,179 ft summit. It is non-technical but steep and demanding, and needs an ice axe, crampons, a helmet and solid self-arrest skills. Most parties take two days with a high camp at Helen Lake; fit parties do it in one long push.
routes.beta: From Helen Lake, climb straight up Avalanche Gulch on snow, heading between the dark rock of The Heart on the left and Thumb Rock on the right. The slope steepens toward the Red Banks, the band of reddish volcanic cliffs at around 12,800 ft and the crux of the route. Most parties climb one of the steep snow or ice chutes that cut through the Red Banks; others go right toward Thumb Rock and climb around the end of the Red Banks, which is more exposed to the ridge and wind. Above the Red Banks, a short climb leads to the base of Misery Hill (about 13,000 ft and up), a long, tiring slope that feels like a false summit. From its top, cross the flat summit plateau and scramble up the small rocky summit pinnacle.
routes.approach: From Bunny Flat, follow the trail up through red fir forest to Horse Camp and the stone Sierra Club cabin at about 7,900 ft, which has a spring and camping. Above Horse Camp, follow Olberman's Causeway, a path of laid stones, above tree line, then continue up past Spring Hill and 50/50 Flat into lower Avalanche Gulch. Keep climbing on snow to Helen Lake at about 10,400 ft, a broad flat bench in the gulch and the usual high camp. The lake itself is buried under snow for most of the climbing season.
routes.descent_text: Descend the same route. When the snow is soft enough, many climbers glissade long sections of the gulch, but always take crampons off first and keep the ice axe ready to brake. In poor visibility it is easy to drift east off the route into Mud Creek Canyon, so navigate carefully on the way down.
routes.turnaround: Set a firm turnaround time before leaving camp and keep to it, so that you are back down through the Red Banks before the snow softens and rockfall picks up. Turn back early if the weather changes or anyone shows signs of altitude sickness.
routes.bail: The whole route can be reversed at any point back down the gulch to Helen Lake and Bunny Flat. Anyone with altitude sickness symptoms should head down straight away.
routes.itinerary: Day 1: Bunny Flat to Helen Lake via Horse Camp and Olberman's Causeway, and set up high camp. Day 2: Alpine start from Helen Lake, climb through the Red Banks and over Misery Hill to the summit, then descend to camp, pack up and walk out to Bunny Flat. Single-day parties leave Bunny Flat in the very early hours and climb the whole route in one push.

pitch_detail.notes: Forested trail to the Sierra Club cabin at about 7,900 ft; spring water and camping.
Olberman's Causeway above tree line, then past Spring Hill and 50/50 Flat up the gulch to Helen Lake at about 10,400 ft.

pitch_detail.pitch: Helen Lake to the Red Banks
pitch_detail.notes: Straight up Avalanche Gulch between The Heart and Thumb Rock; slopes steepen toward the Red Banks around 12,800 ft.
The crux. Climb one of the chutes through the cliffs, or go right around the end near Thumb Rock.
A long, tiring slope above 13,000 ft that looks like the summit but is not.
Cross the flat plateau and scramble up the small rocky summit pinnacle at 14,179 ft.

what_to_bring: Extra layer or durable pants for glissading
Stove and fuel for melting snow
obj_haz: Rockfall from the Red Banks and upper gulch, worse as the sun warms the slope and as the season goes on
Hard, icy snow in the morning where a slip can turn into a long slide
Avalanche danger after storms and in winter and spring
High winds and sudden storms high on the mountain
routes.watch_out:
Descending too far east into Mud Creek Canyon in poor visibility
Glissading with crampons on
Mistaking Misery Hill for the summit and running out of energy or time
Headaches, nausea or confusion from altitude
pro_tips: Start very early so you climb on firm snow and descend before it gets soft and rockfall increases
Wear your helmet from Helen Lake upward
Save energy for Misery Hill, which is longer than it looks
Check the avalanche and climbing advisory before you go

road.name: Everitt Memorial Highway
road.status: Paved; plowed to Bunny Flat year-round
road.driveNote: From the town of Mount Shasta, drive about 11-12 miles up Everitt Memorial Highway to the Bunny Flat parking area, which has restrooms. The road is plowed to Bunny Flat all year; the gate above it opens only after the snow melts.

timing.recommendedStart: Around 2 a.m. for a summit day from Helen Lake or a single-day push from Bunny Flat

bivy.name: Horse Camp
bivy.notes: Near the stone Sierra Club cabin just below tree line, with spring water; a small camping fee applies.

bivy.name: Helen Lake
bivy.notes: The usual high camp for a two-day climb: a broad, flat bench in Avalanche Gulch, usually snow-covered and exposed to wind. Above 10,000 ft, so a Summit Pass is required to camp here.

access.permit: Free wilderness permit for everyone entering the Mount Shasta Wilderness, plus a Summit Pass for everyone going above 10,000 ft, even if you do not plan to reach the summit. Both can be self-issued at the Bunny Flat trailhead kiosk or picked up at the Mount Shasta or McCloud ranger stations. Rangers check passes on the mountain. All human waste must be packed out; free pack-out bags are available at trailheads and ranger stations. Group size is limited to 10 and dogs are not allowed in the wilderness.
access.fees: Wilderness permit free; Summit Pass $25 for 3 days or $30 for an annual pass
